originalTitle: Transplanted pig kidney works in US man's body for record 271 days
summary: A man has lived for a record nine months with a transplanted pig kidney while waiting for a human transplant.
content:
Patient Tim Andrews (centre) with Dr Tatsuo Kawai (left) and Dr Leonardo Riella (right)

A kidney transplanted from a pig has worked inside a patient for 271 days – the longest on record, say US doctors.

Tim Andrews said the transplant gave him "hope" and spared him months of needing to go to hospital to have his blood filtered by a dialysis machine.

The team at Mass General Brigham hospital say their work shows pig organs can be used as a "bridge" until a human transplant becomes available.

But the pig organ eventually failed and was removed so Andrews needed a short bout of dialysis before a donor was found.

Doctors and scientists are exploring xenotransplantation – using organs from other species – due to shortages of organs for transplants.

In the US, around 100,000 people are waiting for a kidney while only 25,000 transplants occur each year. More than 7,000 people in the UK are on the kidney transplant list.

Andrews was told it could take seven years to get to the top of the list, but that people live only five years, on average, on dialysis.

"I had a little bit of a shortage of time… it becomes very depressing," he said.

But he described the idea of a pig transplant as "hope" and the "light at the end of the tunnel".

"Hope is the biggest thing, the chance to be free from the [dialysis] machine and live your life."

Tim Andrews preparing for surgery in January 2025

The donor kidney had been harvested from a genetically modified pig to make it suitable for human donation

Surgeons attached the pig kidney to the blood vessels inside Tim Andrews' body so the organ could filter the blood.

An emotional Tim Andrews and his wife Karen share an embrace while leaving Massachusetts General Hospital on Feb 1, 2025

Pigs are seen as the ideal animal for xenotransplantation. Their organs are roughly the right size and there have been years of experience farming them.

But you cannot just pop down to the farm and take a kidney from a pig and put it into a person. The human body would immediately identify the organ as foreign and launch a devastating immune assault that would destroy the kidney. It would turn black in minutes as holes are ripped in every cell and the organ clots from the inside.

So researchers have developed Yucatan miniature pigs that have gone through 69 genomic modifications to "humanise" their organs.

These modifications strip out some features of pig cells that our immune system spots and attacks; add some human DNA that acts like camouflage netting to help hide the pig tissue from the immune system and further tweaks disable viruses that hide inside pig DNA to prevent infection.

Are pigs the future of organ transplants?

Andrews had end stage kidney disease as a result of type 2 diabetes and his kidney's were failing.

He was 66 years old when he had the xenotransplant on January 25, 2025.

The transplanted pig kidney worked immediately, according to details just published in the Lancet medical journal , external .

The kidney continued to function for 271 days until it was removed in October that year. Tim then needed dialysis for 82 days until he had an organ from a donor in January of this year. That organ has been working well.

Dr Leonardo Riella, from the centre for transplantation sciences at Mass General Brigham said the shortage of organs available for transplant meant " we are in a crisis".

"We are working really hard to bring hope and we truly feel that xenotransplantation can be an alternative for patients who don't have a living donor where we could potentially bypass dialysis and get them to a transplant," he said.

Man who received first pig kidney transplant dies

There were early signs Andrews' organ was being rejected by the immune system, but that was successfully treated by adjusting his medication.

However, after around six months the blood vessels in the kidney started to become damaged and the organ inflamed and then it started to fail.

It is not clear exactly why as there were no signs of antibodies attacking the pig kidney.

In their Lancet write-up the doctors state: "This case illustrates both the promise and the remaining challenges of clinical kidney xenotransplantation."
chineseTitle: 移植猪肾在美国男子体内发挥作用创纪录271天
chineseSummary: 一名男子在等待人体移植期间，通过移植的猪肾存活了创纪录的九个月。
chineseContent:
患者 Tim Andrews（中）与 Tatsuo Kawai 医生（左）和 Leonardo Riella 医生（右）

美国医生称，从猪身上移植的肾脏已在患者体内工作了 271 天，这是有记录以来最长的记录。

蒂姆·安德鲁斯说，移植手术给了他“希望”，让他免去了几个月去医院用透析机过滤血液的时间。

麻省总医院布里格姆医院的研究小组表示，他们的工作表明猪器官可以用作人体移植之前的“桥梁”。

但猪的器官最终失败并被移除，因此安德鲁斯在找到捐赠者之前需要进行短暂的透析。

由于移植器官短缺，医生和科学家正在探索异种移植——使用其他物种的器官。

在美国，大约有 100,000 人正在等待肾脏移植，而每年仅进行 25,000 例移植手术。英国有超过7000人在肾移植名单上。

安德鲁斯被告知可能需要七年时间才能跻身榜首，但人们靠透析平均只能活五年。

“我有点缺乏时间……这变得非常令人沮丧，”他说。

但他将猪移植的想法描述为“希望”和“隧道尽头的光明”。

“希望是最重要的事情，是摆脱[透析]机器并过上自己生活的机会。”

蒂姆·安德鲁斯 (Tim Andrews) 为 2025 年 1 月的手术做准备

供体肾脏是从转基因猪身上摘取的，使其适合人类捐赠

外科医生将猪肾连接到蒂姆·安德鲁斯体内的血管上，以便该器官可以过滤血液。

2025 年 2 月 1 日，情绪激动的蒂姆·安德鲁斯 (Tim Andrews) 和他的妻子凯伦 (Karen) 在离开马萨诸塞州总医院时拥抱

猪被视为异种移植的理想动物。它们的器官大小大致合适，并且有多年的养殖经验。

但你不能直接跑到农场，从猪身上取出一个肾脏，然后把它植入到人体内。人体会立即将该器官识别为异物，并发起毁灭性的免疫攻击，摧毁肾脏。随着每个细胞都被撕裂，器官从内部凝结，它会在几分钟内变黑。

因此，研究人员培育出了尤卡坦半岛小型猪，它们经过了 69 项基因组修饰，使其器官“人性化”。

这些修饰去除了我们的免疫系统发现和攻击的猪细胞的一些特征；添加一些人类 DNA，其作用类似于伪装网，以帮助隐藏猪组织免受免疫系统的侵害，并进一步调整以禁用隐藏在猪 DNA 内的病毒以防止感染。

猪是器官移植的未来吗？

安德鲁斯因 2 型糖尿病而患有终末期肾病，并且他的肾脏正在衰竭。

2025年1月25日进行异种移植时，他已经66岁了。

根据刚刚发表在《柳叶刀》医学杂志《外部》上的详细信息，移植的猪肾立即发挥作用。

肾脏继续发挥功能271天，直到当年10月被摘除。蒂姆随后需要进行 82 天的透析，直到今年 1 月获得捐赠者的器官。该器官一直运转良好。

麻省总医院移植科学中心的莱昂纳多·里埃拉博士表示，可供移植的器官短缺意味着“我们正处于危机之中”。

他说：“我们正在非常努力地带来希望，我们确实认为异种移植可以成为没有活体捐赠者的患者的替代方案，我们可以绕过透析并让他们接受移植。”

首次接受猪肾移植的男子去世

有早期迹象表明安德鲁斯的器官被免疫系统排斥，但通过调整药物治疗成功治愈了这种情况。

然而，大约六个月后，肾脏中的血管开始受损，器官发炎，然后开始衰竭。

目前还不清楚具体原因，因为没有任何抗体攻击猪肾的迹象。

医生们在《柳叶刀》的文章中指出：“这个案例说明了临床肾异种移植的前景和剩余的挑战。”
